description.summary: A Japanese cat yokai that gains supernatural powers after living a long time or growing to an unusual size. Bakeneko can shape-shift into human form, speak human language, walk on hind legs, and possess various magical abilities.
description.full: Bakeneko (化け猫, 'monster cat') is a type of Japanese yokai, or supernatural creature, that was once an ordinary cat. According to traditional folklore, cats that live for many years (commonly cited as 10-13 years), grow to an unusually large size, or develop a long tail can transform into bakeneko. These supernatural cats possess various powers including shape-shifting into human form, speaking human language, walking upright on their hind legs, controlling fire, animating the dead (necromancy), and cursing humans. Bakeneko are particularly known for their ability to impersonate murdered humans with uncanny accuracy. While some bakeneko act malevolently—often seeking revenge for mistreatment—others are simply mischievous. A distinctive behavior is their fondness for eating lamp oil. The folklore surrounding bakeneko led to the historical practice of cutting cats' tails short to prevent transformation, contributing to the development of the Japanese Bobtail breed. Bakeneko are distinct from nekomata, though the terms are sometimes used interchangeably; nekomata are generally more powerful and possess two tails.
